name: Should I hire a designer or contractor first for a bathroom remodel?

mainEntity.name: Should I hire a designer or contractor first for a bathroom remodel, especially for a high-end project?
mainEntity.text: Should I hire a designer or contractor first for a bathroom remodel, especially for a high-end project?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a high-end bathroom remodel, starting with a clear design direction usually leads to better results. That does not always mean hiring a designer before a contractor, but it does mean the layout, finishes, and budget should be developed together early. If you get contractor pricing too soon, the estimate may be based on incomplete selections and later rise when the real materials are chosen. If you design too far without contractor input, the plan may become expensive or impractical. The best approach is usually to define the vision, assemble a realistic material direction, and then confirm buildability and cost with a contractor who understands the space. This is especially helpful in Los Angeles-area homes where older conditions, permits, and custom finishes can affect the final plan. For complex bathrooms, coordinated design and construction planning saves time and reduces redesign later.
acceptedAnswer.description: For a high-end bathroom remodel, it often helps to define the design vision first and then price the project with a contractor. If the project is complex, design and construction planning should be aligned early so the layout, materials, and budget are realistic before work begins.
